jobs.description:
Brady Corporation is seeking an experienced Senior Electrical Engineer to join our Engineering team. In this role, you will lead the design and development of the circuit boards that control our industrial laser marking systems. You will take ownership of existing controller designs and help define the hardware for our next generation of products, working across the full development lifecycle from concept and design to testing, production, and ongoing support.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree or higher in Electrical Engineering or related field.
* 8+ years of experience designing PCBs for embedded or industrial products.
* Proficiency in schematic capture and PCB layout using Altium Designer; OrCAD/Allegro experience is a plus.
* Experience with high-speed digital and mixed-signal design, and with power circuits such as DC-DC converters.
* Knowledge of EMC/EMI design principles and circuit protection.
* Hands-on lab skills for board bring-up and debugging.
* Experience with safety circuits, motion control, or laser systems is a plus.

  
Req Benefits:

* Comprehensive insurance coverage starting on your first day of employment, including medical, dental, and vision

* Education reimbursement opportunities

* A variety of Employee Resource Groups to provide you with unique networking, development, and volunteer opportunities
* Employee Assistance Program and related wellness programs (mental and behavioral health, family counseling, financial management)
* Dress-for-your-day dress code
* Charitable contributions matched through Brady's Matching Gift program

  
Additional Details :

**Who we are:**  

Brady Corporation is a global industrial technology leader dedicated to making workplaces safer, more productive, and more connected. Backed by a 110+ year legacy of reliability and innovation, we have entered an exciting era of transformation and growth, powered by more than 10,000 team members serving customers across 40+ countries. Following our acquisition of Honeywell's Productivity Solutions and Services business in August 2026, Brady brings together trusted leadership in safety, materials science, and identification with advanced mobile computing, scanning, and automation.

We help organizations make work safer, more productive, and more connected by transforming everyday critical information into actionable intelligence. Our end-to-end platform unites two powerful pillars:

* Identification Solutions: High-performance labels, safety signs, engineered materials, and rugged industrial printing systems.
* Intelligent Productivity Solutions: Industry-leading mobile computers, barcode/RFID scanners, specialized software, voice automation, and workflow services.

From aerospace, healthcare, and laboratories to manufacturing plants, retail, data centers, and global transportation and logistics hubs, we empower customers to identify, protect, track, and optimize the people, assets, and processes that keep the world running.

**Why work at Brady:**  
A career at Brady means working for a global company that has thrived for over 100 years, and whose innovative spirit drives our future growth.

Brady offers competitive pay and great benefits, supported by a culture that encourages collaboration and innovation. We strive to foster an inclusive workplace where diverse talent can learn, grow, and succeed. And with deeply rooted values, no matter where you work at Brady, you'll feel connected to the community through our charitable contributions and opportunities to give back.

Our headquarters are in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, but we have more than 70 locations globally, giving our employees the opportunity to work with colleagues around the world.

We want to make powerful AI as accessible as the personal computer. To do that, we need to turn our technology into a well designed physical product that people can put on their desks, plug in, and use every day.

We are looking for an electrical engineer who can take an idea and turn it into reality. You’ll take a high ownership over a large amount of work: schematic capture, layout, routing, validation, characterization, and high-level work across teams to develop the hardware that brings our AI platform into people's homes and businesses.

This is a role for someone who loves electronics, hacking, and building things. The kind of people that grew up watching Linus Tech Tips, rooting their phone, and playing around with Luckypatcher. You should be excited about designing a PCB, figuring out thermals and power delivery, and making a product that can change the world. You'll own the process of rapidly prototyping, testing, and iterating on our hardware until it's ready to manufacture.

**What you’ll do:**
-------------------

* **Own the hardware stack:** Design, assemble, and iterate on complete computer systems, from component selection to working prototypes.
* **Develop electronics:** Schematic capture, layout, routing, power delivery, wiring, and custom electronics for our products.
* **Engineer a system:** Integrate compute, memory, storage, networking, firmware, and operating systems into reliable hardware.
* **Prepare for production:** Refine designs for cost, reliability, manufacturability, and eventual large-scale assembly. If you’re willing, you may be able to go to Shenzhen.

**Who we’re looking for:**
--------------------------

* **Passion for electronics:** You care about performance, cost, reliability, and can balance engineering tradeoffs to build a great product. You spend your free time on tech youtube and hacking with random electronics.
* **Electrical engineering fundamentals:** Experience with circuit design, schematic capture, PCB design (layout + routing), soldering, and electronics prototyping. You must be well-versed in either KiCad, Altium, or Allegro.
* **Computer systems knowledge:** Strong understanding of PC hardware, storage, networking, and hardware/software integration.
* **Hands-on prototyping:** Comfortable assembling, testing, debugging, and modifying hardware, from individual circuits to complete computers.
* **Software skills:** Experience with Python, C/C++, Linux scripting, or low-level systems programming for hardware bring-up and automation.
* **Independence:** You can take an ambiguous idea, figure out how to make it real, and build it with minimal direction.

**How to apply:**
-----------------

Send us your resume and examples of projects you've designed or built, along with a short note about why Alpaca interests you.

More than credentials, we want to see what you've made, researched, designed, or shipped.

If the role sounds like you but your background is unconventional, apply anyway.

Compensation Range: $140K - $170K

jobs.description:
Motional is a leading autonomous driving company on a mission to make driverless vehicles a safe, reliable, and accessible reality. Backed by Hyundai Motor Group, Motional is at the forefront of the physical AI revolution. Motional isn't just building first-of-its-kind technology; we are transforming transportation to create safer streets and more sustainable mobility options.

The Systems Readiness and Performance team is the crucial bridge between software development and real-world deployment. We are responsible for driving system design, for verifying and validating the autonomy stack, and for defining, measuring, and validating system performance targets. We work closely with stakeholders in autonomy, vehicle platform, safety, infrastructure, and operations to build the safety case for our fully driverless IONIQ 5 robotaxis in Las Vegas and to shape the vehicle platform that comes next.

  

**Mission Summary:**

Motional is defining its next-generation robotaxi platform together with Hyundai Motor Group. The requirements we deliver over the coming year will set how the autonomy software commands and monitors the vehicle: steering, braking, propulsion, redundant command paths, and behavior under faults. These decisions are hard to change once the vehicle is designed, and getting them right early is one of the highest-leverage things we can do for the program.

As Principal Engineer, you will own Motional's vehicle control and interface requirements for this platform and be our lead systems engineering voice with Hyundai Motor Group's vehicle engineers. We are looking for someone who has done this before: brought up a new vehicle platform for an automated driving or ADAS system, lived with the consequences of early interface decisions, and knows what to ask for the second time around. You will draw on that experience and on what we learned deploying our current fleet, drive the key architecture trade-offs to a decision, and carry the requirements through to verification on prototype vehicles.

  

**What you'll be doing:**

* Own the vehicle control and interface requirements for Motional's next-generation platform, from first draft through release and verification.
* Lead technical engagement with Hyundai Motor Group's vehicle engineering teams, including in-person workshops in Korea, and drive open questions to closure.
* Lead trade studies on control interface architecture (for example, torque and steering angle commands versus acceleration or trajectory-level interfaces) and bring stakeholders to a decision backed by data.
* Turn lessons learned from our current fleet into clear, verifiable requirements on the vehicle platform and on the signals it reports back to the autonomy system.
* Work with Safety and the vehicle platform team on the functional safety concept for the control path: redundancy, fault handling, degraded operation, and arbitration with base-vehicle safety functions.
* Partner with Sourcing on the vehicle interface controller supplier: requirements, acceptance criteria, and schedule risk.
* Maintain the system description, interface definitions, traceability, and verification strategy for the vehicle interface subsystem.
* Set technical direction and mentor systems engineers working on vehicle control.
  

**What we're looking for:**

* BS in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Robotics, Computer, or equivalent Engineering; MS preferred.
* 10+ years of engineering experience, including at least one full vehicle platform bring-up for an ADAS or automated driving system: defining the interface to a new vehicle, working through prototype builds with the automaker or supplier, and taking the platform to validated operation.
* Hands-on experience with vehicle motion control or drive-by-wire systems (propulsion, braking, steering), and with writing and negotiating interface requirements with an automaker or Tier 1 supplier.
* Working knowledge of automotive functional safety (ISO 26262) applied to vehicle control: safety goals, ASIL allocation, fault handling, and degraded modes.
* Strong analytical skills across vehicle dynamics, data analysis, and systems analysis.
* Excellent written and verbal communication; effective at driving decisions across organizations and cultures.
* Ability to read C++ control software; Python or similar for data analysis.
* Experience leading cross-team technical work and mentoring engineers.
  

**Bonus points(not required):**

* Experience bringing up more than one vehicle platform, or platforms from more than one automaker.
* Familiarity with automotive E/E architectures and in-vehicle networking (CAN, Automotive Ethernet).
* Supplier management experience (statements of work, sample acceptance, joint testing).
* Hardware-in-the-loop or test track development for vehicle control systems.
* Korean language proficiency.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, talk, or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand and at times for long periods; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and move up to 50 pounds.

  

**Travel Requirements (greater than 20%)**:

Expected to travel to Korea for engineering workshops and to our Las Vegas, Pittsburgh and Boston sites as needed for the business.

jobs.description:
**Overview**
------------

At Ford, you’ll work on ideas that matter, alongside passionate people who want to make a global impact. Together, we’re shaping the next era of transportation—grounded in purpose, driven by progress. Make your move.

* Job Type: Full time
* Work Type: Hybrid

  

We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.

**In this position...**

The Chassis Systems Engineer is responsible for integrating chassis components into a vehicle-level system to deliver Ford vehicle performance targets. This role partners closely with D&R engineers, Vehicle Engineering, Vehicle Dynamics, and cross-functional teams to establish vehicle kinematic and compliance targets, maintain system health chart documentation, and support development milestones. As the single point of contact for suspension hardpoints and the vehicle ADAMS CAE model, this engineer ensures chassis-related data, models, and test outputs align with program requirements across prototype, launch, and production builds.

**What you'll do...**

* Serve as the single point of contact for suspension hardpoints and the vehicle ADAMS CAE model
* Assess Chassis Systems health chart metrics at each milestone and work with component engineers to close gaps and meet requirements
* Coordinate durability vehicle preparation and testing, ensuring part pedigree matches the CAE model
* Lead problem-solving efforts for chassis component issues, translating test data into actionable engineering recommendations
* Support testing, prototype builds, launch builds, and ongoing production of Ford Racing vehicles at assembly plants and test facilities
* Set targets for vehicle ride height and alignment and evaluate status at vehicle builds
* Cascade travel and check load requirements to shock and spring suppliers
* Interface daily with a global team of D&R engineers, vehicle attribute teams, program management, suppliers, and manufacturing to ensure compliance with specifications and drive efficient critical decisions
* Support vehicle development and supplier reviews, including occasional travel as required

**You'll have.**..

* Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering
* Demonstrated results in chassis systems, vehicle dynamics, vehicle architecture, or suspension component engineering, with experience across different phases of the vehicle product lifecycle
* Experience with ADAMS vehicle dynamics CAE modeling software
* Strong knowledge of chassis systems and how they interface with other vehicle systems
Excellent written and oral communication skills  

**Even Better, You May Have..**.

* Familiarity with Ford PD systems and processes including GPDS, WERS, FEDEBOM, FEDE, Teamcenter, 3DX, etc.
* Experience with vehicle manufacturing launch and prototype processes
* Strong knowledge of tunable suspension component design including shocks, coil springs, bushings, and related mounting hardware
* Familiarity with CAD tools (CATIA)

* A self-starter mentality with the ability to deliver results and overcome obstacles

Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? * Immediate medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage

This position is a salary grade 5 through grade 8. Salaries can and ranges from $65,100 - $166,200.

jobs.description:
**What We Do**

Spartan Light Metal Products is a family-owned leader in aluminum manufacturing with more than 60 years of experience. We manufacture highly engineered components used in electric and fuel-powered vehicles for leading automakers, including General Motors, Ford, Toyota, and Honda. Our success is built on talented people and a culture grounded in our values, servant leadership, collaboration, safety, and quality.

**WHY SPARTAN?**

**More Than a Paycheck.**

At Spartan, your total rewards go beyond your salary. We want our employees to have opportunities to **earn more, be recognized, grow, and build their future.**

**EARN MORE**

* Short Term Incentive Plan — earning potential of up to 10% of your annual salary
* Additional incentive opportunities, where applicable

**BE RECOGNIZED**

* Rewards & Recognition
* Spartan Achievement Awards
* Service Awards recognizing employee milestones and contributions

**GROW**

* Mentorship and development opportunities
* Tuition reimbursement
* Opportunities to learn new skills and grow your career within Spartan

**BUILD YOUR FUTURE**

* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
* Company-provided life insurance
* HSA employer match for eligible employees
* 401(k) with company match

**Come build your future with Spartan.**

**GENERAL SUMMARY**

The Controls Engineer provides technical expertise, development and support of the controls, automation and industrial networking systems for our manufacturing equipment. This role contributes to the attainment of Spartan’s operational goals/objectives by improved manufacturing efficiency, quality and cost.

**PRINCIPAL DUTIES**

1. Apply engineering knowledge and expertise in providing on-going support for the plant floor related to:

* system controls/PLC’s and their related hardware,
* robot/robotic systems - Fanuc based,
* automated inspection equipment (2D & 3D vision and laser)
* software and equipment, including proper use,
* troubleshooting, problem solving, continuous improvement and training.

2. Maintain involvement and alignment with plant maintenance and engineering teams. Provide guidance to any new equipment, tooling or modifications to existing equipment or tooling that require controls input to ensure all consistency in standards and methods.

3. Utilizing engineering expertise, lead and/or support the Spartan team during new machine design/development and concepts. Carry forward lessons learned and Spartan Standards.

4. Implement standard engineering practices in problem solving and projects. Provide detailed documentation upon project completion along with recommended updates to Spartan Equipment Standards.

5. Provide equipment and system control solutions to achieve Spartan’s manufacturing objectives, which includes the design and engineering of PLC/robot control and modifications for a wide variety of manufacturing production equipment.

6. Lead the design and development of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems for production and operations support equipment.

7. Provide concept oversight to electrical assembly activities such as panel fabrication and component wiring.

8. Support field installation and mechanical/electrical integration of automation equipment, including mounting modules and devices (sensors, valves, drives, junction boxes, panels), coordinating and/or assisting with conduit/cable-tray layout and routing, pulling/terminating/labeling conductors, and performing point-to-point verification during equipment builds, retrofits and launches.

9. Produce and update electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and other industrial CAD drawings/schematics.

10. Wire and integrate new automation devices in legacy or undocumented systems by safely tracing circuits, verifying power/control signals, validating I/O operation, and creating as-built documentation for verified terminations and wiring paths.

11. Maintains updated knowledge of latest technology in robotics, controls, sensors and vision systems. Works with component and equipment suppliers to test and trial new technology that has potential to improve manufacturing operations and provide a competitive advantage.

12. Systems integration of 3rd party equipment and peripherals.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Required:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or related technical field
* 3-5 years controls engineering experience
* 5-10 years maintenance experience
* Working proficiency in one primary platform: Rockwell Automation (Allen-Bradley) PLC/HMI development and support using Studio 5000 / RSLogix **and FactoryTalk**, **and** FANUC robot programming, integration, and troubleshooting (TP programming).

**Preferred:** High volume automotive with automated machining and assembly equipment experience.

jobs.description:
Motional is a leading autonomous driving company on a mission to make driverless vehicles a safe, reliable, and accessible reality. Backed by Hyundai Motor Group, Motional is at the forefront of the physical AI revolution. Motional isn't just building first-of-its-kind technology; we are transforming transportation to create safer streets and more sustainable mobility options.

The Systems Readiness and Performance team is the crucial bridge between software development and real-world deployment. We are responsible for driving system design, for verifying and validating the autonomy stack, and for defining, measuring, and validating system performance targets. We work closely with stakeholders in autonomy, vehicle platform, safety, infrastructure, and operations to build the safety case for our fully driverless IONIQ 5 robotaxis in Las Vegas and to shape the vehicle platform that comes next.

  

**Mission Summary:**

The vehicle control interface is where Motional's autonomy software interfaces with the vehicle platform: steering, braking, and propulsion commands go out, and actuator state, faults, and vehicle interventions come back. Gaps in requirements or test coverage at this boundary show up as issues on the road.

As a Senior Systems Engineer embedded with our vehicle control software team, you will own the verification and validation strategy for the vehicle interface software on our current fleet, act as the systems reviewer for changes going into releases, and contribute to the control interface requirements for our next-generation platform.

  

**What you'll be doing:**

* Build and own the verification and validation plan for the vehicle interface control software: catalog existing tests across unit, integration, simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, and test track; map them to requirements; and close coverage gaps.
* Establish an impact analysis process so every software change ships with the right regression tests identified and tracked.
* Review and approve changes to vehicle interface and fault handling logic as the systems engineering representative, defining the evidence needed for release.
* Analyze fleet and test data to characterize vehicle behavior (braking, traction and stability interventions, torque response) and turn findings into requirements and test cases.
* Draft and review control interface requirements for the next-generation platform alongside the principal engineer, and prepare technical material for discussions with Hyundai Motor Group.
* Support safety analyses on the vehicle control path and make sure the resulting requirements are testable.
* Build automated analysis and dashboards (Python, SQL) that give fast feedback on vehicle interface performance.
* Support root cause analysis of vehicle interface issues from testing and operations.
  

**What we're looking for:**

* BS in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Robotics, Computer, or equivalent Engineering; MS preferred.
* 5+ years of engineering experience on safety-critical systems, including hands-on work bringing up or integrating a vehicle platform for an ADAS or automated driving system (vehicle interface, actuation, drive-by-wire control, or platform testing).
* End-to-end systems engineering experience: requirements, analysis, and verification and validation, including building test plans and tracking requirement-to-test coverage.
* Software or hardware test development experience.
* Strong analytical skills across vehicle dynamics, data analysis, and systems analysis.
* Python or similar, and SQL, for analyzing test and fleet data; ability to read C++.
* Excellent written and verbal communication; effective working day to day with a software development team.
* In-vehicle networking tools and signal definition with CAN
  

**Bonus points(not required):**

* Automotive functional safety or SOTIF experience (ISO 26262, ISO 21448) applied to control software.
* Hardware-in-the-loop test development.
* Requirements management and traceability tools (Jama, DOORS, Polarion, or similar).
* Experience working directly with an automaker or Tier 1 supplier on vehicle interfaces.
  

**Physical Demands:**

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, talk, or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand and at times for long periods; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and move up to 50 pounds.

Expected to travel to our Las Vegas test site and to Pittsburgh for vehicle testing and integration, roughly 1-2 weeks each quarter, with occasional international travel as needed for the business.

The work environment characteristics described here represent those a team member encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. **What Your Job Will Be Like**
------------------------------

  

The opportunity exists for an R&D Systems Engineer to conduct surveillance on the Multiapplication Transportation Attachment Device (MTAD) as part of the Integrated Surety Architectures (ISA) program. Whereas realized nuclear weapon products are typically fielded and rarely used, the MTAD is regularly operating on transportation missions for enhanced over-the-road security. You will have the opportunity to assess MTAD mission performance, support working groups to evaluate the data, and support product reacceptance as part of monitoring state of health while ensuring continued fielding. Your work will impact organizations across Sandia; you will interface with stockpile systems as well as transportation systems i.e. Safeguards Transporter (SGT). As ISA over-the-road missions continue to mature, the program is also establishing common data-management infrastructure, governance, tools, and analytical workflows to support mission surveillance and system assessment. You will serve as a key technical contributor and user of this evolving environment by identifying subsystem data needs, evaluating mission information, supporting data quality and context, and providing MTAD-specific expertise to the Mission Data Working Group. You will be a critical technical team member supporting the development of the governance framework and data coordination across programs.

jobs.title: Enterprise Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
Enterprise Automation Engineering drives efficiency across Datadog through systems automation and integrations, AI agents and MCP development. The team is increasingly embedded in cross-functional initiatives across People, Finance, GTM, Legal, Recruiting, and Technical Solutions — translating ambiguous business problems into scoped, buildable solutions and owning delivery end-to-end.

As a Senior Automation Engineer, you design and build the technical solutions that power Datadog's internal systems. You work closely with BSAs and business stakeholders to take well-scoped requirements and ship production-grade integrations, automations, agents, and internal apps. You will also actively shape how AI and agentic tooling gets embedded into Datadog's internal workflows.

*At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.*

### **What You'll Do:**

* **Build and ship:** Architect, build, and maintain production-grade integrations, automations, agents, and internal apps across Datadog's core business systems — Workday, Greenhouse, NetSuite, Salesforce, and more
* **Lead technical design:** Define data flows, error handling, scalability requirements, and architectural decisions for multi-system workflows
* **Own the AI/agent layer:** Design and develop agentic workflows, MCP servers, and LLM-integrated solutions that extend what the team can deliver
* **Set platform standards:** Define and enforce what production-ready means for internal systems — governance, observability, reliability, and maintainability; help the organization move from vibe-coded prototypes to scalable platforms
* **Advise on build vs. buy:** Evaluate tools and platforms and make recommendations on when to build custom vs. configure existing
* **Ensure compliance:** Collaborate with Security, Privacy, and Compliance to ensure solutions adhere to Datadog's standards — GDPR, SOX, SOC 2, FedRAMP

### **Who You Are:**

* Demonstrated experience building with AI/agentic tools — not just evaluating them; you've shipped something with an LLM, an agent framework, or an MCP and can speak to the tradeoffs
* Strong judgment on build vs. buy, custom vs. configuration
* Able to communicate technical decisions clearly to non-technical stakeholders — you can explain why a design choice matters without losing the room
* Experience working autonomously on a small, high-ownership team at a high-growth company

#### **Senior Business Systems Engineer**

* 5+ years administrating and integrating business systems (e.g., NetSuite, Zendesk, Salesforce or Workday) or in a similar role
* 4+ years leading medium to large sized cross-functional projects across Finance, HR, and Sales
* 3+ years designing and building multi-system integrations using middleware (e.g., Workato, Boomi, Mulesoft, Zapier)
* In-depth knowledge of SQL and object-oriented programming paradigms (e.g., Python, Java) to efficiently manipulate large volumes of data

  

*Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you're passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.*

  

**Benefits and Growth:**

* New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)
* Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing
* Intradepartmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking
* An inclusive company culture, ability to join our Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups)
* Access to Inclusion Talks, our Internal panel discussions
* Free, global mental health benefits for employees and dependents age 6+
* Competitive global benefits

  

*Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.*

  

#LI-HYBRID

**About Datadog:**

Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. It brings applications, infrastructure, data, models, and security into one place, using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers. Trusted globally by Fortune 500 companies and high-growth AI leaders, Datadog enables businesses to move faster with clarity and confidence. Learn more about #DatadogLife on Instagram, LinkedIn, and Datadog Learning Center.

Datadog is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and other characteristics protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. Here are our Candidate Legal Notices for your reference.

Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems (RMS) provides surface, air and undersea applications for U.S. military and international customers. Our vision for RMS is to set performance standards for our customers worldwide, every day with the best people, best systems, and best services.

WHO WE ARE  
In this position, the EMI/EMC Systems Engineer will lead the Electromagnetic Environmental Effects activities and provide EMI design support across multiple programs. jobs.title: Controls Engineer, revengOS
jobs.description:
**About Raglan**

Raglan builds vehicles for today’s and tomorrow’s fight. We engineer mission-critical systems for defense, government, and commercial applications, bringing a warfighter’s perspective to modernizing tactical platforms and developing new capabilities.

Our work spans propulsion, software-defined vehicles, and modular exportable power systems—from open-architecture vehicle control software to hybrid platforms. We work closely with operators, program teams, and engineering partners to turn real-world requirements into systems built for demanding missions.

Based in Wilmington, North Carolina, Raglan is a Veteran-Owned Small Business. We’re looking for people ready to take ownership of the hardest mission-critical mobility challenges.

**The mission**

Join Raglan's on-site engineering team in Wilmington, North Carolina, to build new and modernize existing military ground vehicle control systems with revengOS, helping deliver dependable mobility for the warfighter. You'll develop, integrate, and validate controls for vehicle subsystems, from bench testing through calibration on the dyno and in the vehicle. You'll own well-defined features and subsystem pieces end to end, working alongside senior engineers who set the overall control strategy. This is a hands-on individual contributor role spanning software, hardware, and vehicle integration.

**What you'll do**

* Develop and test control software in MATLAB/Simulink and embedded C/C++ on automotive-grade microcontrollers.
* Implement and refine subsystem controls for diesel and hybrid platforms, such as fueling, torque management, transmission shifting, and power-distribution protection.
* Capture and decode CAN/LIN traffic, scope traces, and wiring to help reverse engineer OEM controller behavior.
* Maintain and extend DBC databases and implement controller communication within the vehicle CAN architecture.
* Integrate and calibrate embedded controller platforms such as OpenECU, Emtron, ECOTRON, STW, MoTeC, TTControl, MotoHawk, Life Racing, New Eagle, and Bosch.
* Run validation on a four-wheel chassis dynamometer and in real operating conditions, logging data and resolving differences between modeled and measured behavior.
* Support wiring harness build and integration for controllers, sensors, and actuators, and troubleshoot hardware, firmware, and vehicle-level faults.

**What you bring**

* A solid understanding of engine and drivetrain operation, including combustion, fueling, torque, and shift mechanics.
* Experience developing controls in MATLAB/Simulink and embedded software in C/C++ on microcontrollers.
* Working CAN skills, including protocol decoding and DBC editing with CAN tools such as Vector CANalyzer, PCAN, or similar.
* Hands-on experience testing, calibrating, or validating controls on a dyno, test bench, or vehicle.
* Comfort working hands-on with vehicles, wiring, and test equipment, and debugging across software and hardware.
* Ability to own assigned features from development through validation, with guidance on overall direction.

**Nice to have**

* Reverse engineering OEM controllers or building aftermarket or standalone control solutions.
* Hybrid / electric vehicle development: torque management, battery management, charging, or export power.
* Transmission control and calibration, including multi-clutch or automatic shift control.
* ABS, traction control, or body and power-distribution control experience.
* Production embedded development involving timing, interrupts, peripherals, or driver-level code.
* Wiring harness design from schematic through build.
* Formula SAE / Baja SAE, motorsport, defense, or other durability-critical vehicle experience.

Don't check every box? If you've done the core of this work, apply anyway.

**Pay & Benefits**

**Base salary:** $135,000–$165,000 (North Carolina)

This is the base salary range we in good faith expect to pay for this role. Where you land depends on your skills and experience, which we assess through the interview process.

**Benefits:**

* Medical, dental, and vision coverage
* 20 days of vacation, plus all federal holidays
* Parental leave
* Professional development support: training, certifications, and conferences

**Export control and security clearance.** This position requires access to classified information and to technical data and items controlled under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and/or the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Applicants must be U.S. citizens and able to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required for clearance eligibility.

**Equal opportunity.** Raglan is an equal opportunity employer. We make employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran or military status, or any other status protected by law. If you need a reasonable accommodation to apply or interview, contact careers@raglan.com.

Raglan participates in E-Verify.

 **The pay range for this role is:**  
135,000 - 165,000 USD per year(Wilmington, NC)

jobs.title: Senior HPC Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
### **About the Company**

We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company's direction on a regular basis.

Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.

### **About the Job**

Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean's harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention.

You will join Panthalassa's Compute Infrastructure team, a small platform engineering team that builds and operates shared infrastructure as internal products. The team owns a Kubernetes-based compute platform on GKE (ArgoCD, GitHub Actions runners, Terraform modules) and is bringing our on-premises HPC clusters under the same model: a managed HPC platform that CFD engineers consume through a documented golden path rather than through ad-hoc requests to an administrator. Your work will directly support our mission to deliver abundant renewable energy and affordable green fuels.

You will own that HPC platform end to end: Linux, Slurm, storage, interconnects, provisioning, and scientific software. Your initial scope is our primary CFD cluster, with the expectation that you grow into ownership of our second cluster and define how both are operated under the same configuration management and operational standards as the rest of our infrastructure.

This is a hands-on role with broad ownership and room to shape how our computing infrastructure grows. You will work closely with CFD engineers on production workloads and performance, and with an on-site datacenter technician who carries out physical hardware work. We are looking for someone who follows problems through to resolution, communicates clearly, and builds systems that others can operate confidently and that engineers can consume without needing to understand how they work underneath.

The services running on these clusters, including scheduling, software environments, storage, and license servers, are products with users. You will treat them that way: measure how they are used, reduce friction, and iterate.

Candidates should have strong interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment in which the best ideas change the company's direction on a regular basis.

### **Responsibilities**

#### **Platform**

* Contribute to defining the HPC platform as a product: its service catalog, service levels, and roadmap, in partnership with CFD engineering leads, and prioritize work by user impact.
* Build the golden path for running simulations: standard job templates, submission tooling, software environment conventions, and documentation that lets a new CFD engineer go from zero to a correctly placed production job without a ticket.
* Replace manual, ticket-driven operations with self-service wherever practical: account and project onboarding, storage allocation, module requests, license visibility, and job diagnostics.
* Instrument platform usage and health (utilization, queue wait, job failure modes, storage growth) and use it to drive capacity planning and roadmap decisions.
* Contribute to shared team tooling and conventions so HPC and cloud compute are operated the same way.
* Design future HPC capacity and workflows with the GKE platform in mind: burst, hybrid scheduling, shared identity, and shared artifact and container registries.

#### **Platform operations**

* Automate cluster configuration with Ansible and Git so system state is reproducible, reviewable, and applied through CI. Manual changes to cluster state are the exception, not the norm.
* Own the day-to-day operation, configuration, and reliability of our HPC clusters, including compute and head nodes, storage, and interconnects.
* Plan and bring up new compute capacity: specify hardware, define rack and network layouts, and provision and validate nodes after installation.
* Administer Slurm end to end, including partitions, QoS, accounting, scheduling policy, and job troubleshooting for CFD engineers.
* Build and maintain scientific software environments, including Environment Modules or Lmod, MPI stacks, and compiler toolchains tuned for our interconnects.
* Manage diskless provisioning with Warewulf, including PXE and UEFI boot, node images, kernel and driver pinning, and firmware lifecycle.
* Operate Omni-Path and InfiniBand fabrics, including subnet management, link health, topology validation, and MPI performance verification.
* Manage BMC and IPMI access, firmware updates, and remote diagnosis of memory, NIC, and storage faults. Coordinate hardware suppliers and RMAs.
* Work with our on-site datacenter technician on hardware installations, drive and DIMM swaps, cabling, and network changes, providing clear diagnoses and precise instructions.
* Administer shared simulation storage, including ZFS pools, NFS exports, scrub and snapshot schedules, capacity planning, and backup coverage.

jobs.description:
Motional is a leading autonomous driving company on a mission to make driverless vehicles a safe, reliable, and accessible reality. Backed by Hyundai Motor Group, Motional is at the forefront of the physical AI revolution. Motional isn't just building first-of-its-kind technology; we are transforming transportation to create safer streets and more sustainable mobility options.

The Systems Readiness and Performance team is the crucial bridge between software development and real-world deployment. We are responsible for driving system design, for verifying and validating the autonomy stack, and for defining, measuring, and validating system performance targets. We work closely with stakeholders in autonomy, vehicle platform, safety, infrastructure, and operations to build the safety case for our fully driverless IONIQ 5 robotaxis in Las Vegas and to shape the vehicle platform that comes next.

  

**Mission Summary:**

The vehicle control interface is where Motional's autonomy software interfaces with the vehicle platform: steering, braking, and propulsion commands go out, and actuator state, faults, and vehicle interventions come back. Gaps in requirements or test coverage at this boundary show up as issues on the road.

As a Senior Systems Engineer embedded with our vehicle control software team, you will own the verification and validation strategy for the vehicle interface software on our current fleet, act as the systems reviewer for changes going into releases, and contribute to the control interface requirements for our next-generation platform.

  

**What you'll be doing:**

* Build and own the verification and validation plan for the vehicle interface control software: catalog existing tests across unit, integration, simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, and test track; map them to requirements; and close coverage gaps.
* Establish an impact analysis process so every software change ships with the right regression tests identified and tracked.
* Review and approve changes to vehicle interface and fault handling logic as the systems engineering representative, defining the evidence needed for release.
* Analyze fleet and test data to characterize vehicle behavior (braking, traction and stability interventions, torque response) and turn findings into requirements and test cases.
* Draft and review control interface requirements for the next-generation platform alongside the principal engineer, and prepare technical material for discussions with Hyundai Motor Group.
* Support safety analyses on the vehicle control path and make sure the resulting requirements are testable.
* Build automated analysis and dashboards (Python, SQL) that give fast feedback on vehicle interface performance.
* Support root cause analysis of vehicle interface issues from testing and operations.
  

**What we're looking for:**

* BS in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Robotics, Computer, or equivalent Engineering; MS preferred.
* 5+ years of engineering experience on safety-critical systems, including hands-on work bringing up or integrating a vehicle platform for an ADAS or automated driving system (vehicle interface, actuation, drive-by-wire control, or platform testing).
* End-to-end systems engineering experience: requirements, analysis, and verification and validation, including building test plans and tracking requirement-to-test coverage.
* Software or hardware test development experience.
* Strong analytical skills across vehicle dynamics, data analysis, and systems analysis.
* Python or similar, and SQL, for analyzing test and fleet data; ability to read C++.
* Excellent written and verbal communication; effective working day to day with a software development team.
* In-vehicle networking tools and signal definition with CAN

* Automotive functional safety or SOTIF experience (ISO 26262, ISO 21448) applied to control software.
* Hardware-in-the-loop test development.
* Requirements management and traceability tools (Jama, DOORS, Polarion, or similar).
* Experience working directly with an automaker or Tier 1 supplier on vehicle interfaces.

jobs.description:
Overview:

Are you someone who is passionate, motivated, and driven to make a difference? If so, MSA Safety is the perfect fit for your career.

At MSA, SAFETY is who we are AND it is what we do. We are a purpose-driven company committed to deploying innovation and technology to deliver on our Mission to help protect people and assets all around the world. We continue to be relentless in our pursuit of solving our customers greatest problems so they can go home safe each and every day.

Are you in? Read on for more details about this particular role.

Responsibilities:

* Plan, set up, execute, troubleshoot, and document EMC compliance and pre-compliance tests, including radiated and conducted emissions, ESD, EFT/burst, surge, and conducted and radiated RF immunity. This hands-on laboratory work will represent the primary focus of the role.
* Perform selected wireless OTA and radio-performance evaluations, verify test configurations and repeatability, analyze results, and support troubleshooting of connected products using internal RF test capabilities.
* Support EMC engineering throughout the product development lifecycle, with emphasis on test planning, sample and configuration readiness, verification execution, results analysis, and evaluation of product changes.
* Develop clear EMC test plans, procedures, setup records, test logs, engineering analyses, and test reports that provide accurate, traceable, and reusable technical evidence.
* Analyze EMC failures by identifying noise sources, coupling paths, and susceptible circuits; work with design teams to develop, prototype, and verify practical mitigations.
* Work with product development teams to design and improve electronic circuits, interfaces, grounding, shielding, filtering, transient protection, and PCB implementations for EMC, ESD, EFT, surge, RF, and signal-integrity robustness.
* Participate in electrical, PCB, mechanical, cable, and system design reviews; identify EMC risks early and recommend practical design improvements before hardware is released.
* Use circuit and electromagnetic simulation where appropriate to evaluate EMC filters, protection circuits, PCB structures, coupling paths, signal/power integrity, and design alternatives before physical testing.
* Interpret applicable IEC, CISPR, FCC, and product-specific EMC requirements and translate them into actionable design and verification requirements.
* Collaborate with the EMC laboratory technical manager, technician, RF engineering, product compliance, quality, and external laboratories to efficiently complete verification and certification activities.
* Help build organizational EMC capability through mentoring, design guidance, reference designs, technical training, and documented best practices.

Qualifications:

### **Required Skills and Abilities**

* Demonstrated experience designing or evaluating electronic hardware for EMC robustness, including grounding, filtering, shielding, interface protection, component selection, and PCB implementation.
* Substantial hands-on experience independently setting up and performing EMC emissions and immunity testing, pre-compliance testing, hardware troubleshooting, and compliance verification.
* Strong understanding of EMC fundamentals, noise sources, coupling mechanisms, susceptibility, and practical mitigation techniques.
* Ability to read and review electrical schematics and PCB layouts and work effectively with product design teams on design improvements.
* Demonstrated proficiency operating common electronic and EMC test instrumentation such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers or EMI receivers, signal generators, probes, transient generators, RF immunity systems, and associated automation software.
* Ability to develop test plans, technical reports, design guidance, and clear engineering documentation.
* Strong analytical problem-solving, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills; able to independently manage complex technical assignments.
* Minimal travel required (less than 10%), including occasional support at external laboratories.

### **Preferred Skills and Experience**

* Experience with global EMC standards and product certification, including IEC, CISPR, FCC, or related commercial-product requirements.
* Experience with circuit, PCB, SI/PI, or electromagnetic simulation tools such as Ansys SIwave, HFSS, SPICE, CST, or COMSOL.
* Experience with Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro, or similar schematic and PCB design environments.
* Experience with wireless products, intentional radiators, RF/OTA testing, antennas, cellular, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or sub-GHz technologies.
* Experience working in semi-anechoic, fully anechoic, OTA, or shielded test environments.
* Experience with intrinsically safe or other regulated electronic safety products is a plus; iNARTE EMC certification or equivalent professional development is also a plus.

**Education and Experience**
----------------------------

Kipp & Zonen is the specialist in the measurement of solar and sky radiation, from the ultraviolet to the far infrared. **Intermediate Electrical Engineer**

**McCoy Global**

**IF YOU** ACT LIKE AN OWNER AND OWN YOUR ACTIONS;

**IF YOU** EMBRACE CHALLENGE AND LEAD CHANGE;

**IF YOU** EVOLVE, ADAPT AND CELEBRATE SUCCESS;

**IF YOU** APPROACH ALL INTERACTIONS POSTIVELY, COURAGEOULSY AND HONESTLY;

**What We Need:**

Are you passionate about creating innovative technology that performs in some of the world's toughest operating environments? We are seeking an **Intermediate Electrical Engineer** to help design, develop, and test embedded systems that power our industrial sensor and control products.

In this role, you'll work across the entire product development lifecycle, contributing from concept and prototyping through validation, testing, and production release. You'll apply your expertise in embedded hardware and firmware development to build reliable, high-performing solutions that enable our customers to operate safely and efficiently.

As part of a collaborative engineering team, you'll develop software for microcontrollers and microprocessors, contribute to electronic circuit design, troubleshoot complex technical challenges, and help bring new products to market. If you're a hands-on engineer who enjoys solving problems, learning new technologies, and working on products that make a real impact in industrial environments, we'd like to hear from you.

**What you’ll bring:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

**What you’ll do:**

* Hands-on experience programming microcontrollers and microprocessors across common architectures.

* Working knowledge of common hardware interfaces and peripherals (timers, analog I/O, serial communication buses).

**Who Are We?**

Over a century ago, blacksmith Henry McCoy established the Edmonton Auto Spring Works in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. Back in 1914, the name McCoy meant a commitment to quality; and that, along with a desire to continually innovate, is what we stand for today.

**KEEPING AHEAD OF THE CURVE**

Always ahead of the curve, we’ve evolved from auto springs, axle manufacturing, trucking, and trailers, to hydraulic power tongs, advanced engineering for wellbore integrity, data acquisition for harsh environments, and cloud-based automated Smart technology solutions. **When you work at McCoy, you work with:**

* A great teamwork environment that challenges your ability while having fun.
* A voice to help us continuously improve our processes and teams.
* A chance to help us deliver innovative solutions to our customers provide energy to the world.
* An opportunity to grow within our company as we succeed in growing our customers.
* An organization that recognizes and cares about its employee’s well-being.

**So, what can McCoy offer you?**

* We offer competitive time-off
* 4 wellness days PER YEAR plus your birthday off!
* 3 weeks of vacation accrued throughout the year
* We match your 401K
* Matching Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP)
* Work with a company that CARES

**We are 1-McCoy and We want YOU!**

jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Senior Electrical Engineer, Sustaining

**Department:** Hardware Engineering

**Employment Type:** Full-Time

**FLSA Status:** Exempt

**Location:** Houston, TX (on-site)

**Travel:** 10%

**Who We Are**

Persona is building humanoid robots for the most demanding environments in heavy industry — shipyards, steel mills, fabrication facilities, and offshore platforms — performing welding, grinding, maintenance, inspection, and material-handling work that is dangerous, physically demanding, and increasingly difficult to staff.

We are backed by leading strategic and financial investors and engaged with global industrial leaders across Korea, Japan, the United States, and Singapore. Korea is the center of gravity for our early commercial strategy, anchored by relationships with the world’s leading shipbuilders and steelmakers. Our work spans both the robot platform itself and the systems, partners, and playbooks required to deploy it at scale.

**Why Join Persona?**

* We offer competitive compensation, a performance-based bonus, 100% employer covered medical benefits for most healthcare plans, early-stage equity, competitive PTO, and company-wide paid winter break between December 24th and January 2nd.
* You’ll shape technology that’s redefining the possibilities of robotics and human interaction.
* Work alongside passionate teammates who value creativity, and continuous learning.

**About the Role**

We’re looking for a Senior Sustaining Electrical Engineer to own the electronics we already have deployed on our robots. As we scale production, this role ensures our deployed and in-production designs stay healthy, easy to build, and flexible enough to meet new customer needs.

You will sit between our product-focused design engineers and our manufacturing and field operations teams. When a board fails on the line, a robot misbehaves in the field, or a customer application needs something added or done differently, you are the person who troubleshoots it, finds the root cause, and drives the fix — whether that’s a rework, a component change, a design modification, or a documentation update.

This is not a forward-looking design role. It’s a role for an experienced, hands-on engineer who thrives on variety, can juggle many inputs at once, and has the people skills to work across manufacturing, field ops, firmware, and design teams. Expect broad scope and lots of different problems: you’ll often be the filter and the bridge that closes the gap between manufacturing and operations.

If you’ve supported products through their lifecycle and enjoy making shipped hardware work better at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

**What You Will Be Doing**

* Own deployed electrical designs across the robot — PCBAs, harnesses, and rigid-flex assemblies for actuators, sensors, perception, compute, and power — keeping them reliable, manufacturable, and supportable through their lifecycle.
* Serve as the primary electrical interface to manufacturing and field operations: triage incoming issues, prioritize across many inputs, and act as the filter between production, ops, and the product design team.
* Troubleshoot and root-cause failures on the production line and in the field, from board-level faults to full-robot system issues, using schematics, firmware knowledge, and lab tools (scope, logic analyzer, DMM).
* Develop and implement fixes: reworks, component substitutions, ECOs, and targeted design modifications to existing boards.
* Adapt existing designs for new or varied customer applications when something needs to be added or done differently.
* Support the battery and battery management system (BMS) in the field and in production, including diagnostics and corrective actions.
* Partner with manufacturing and EMS partners on yield, DFM/DFA/DFT improvements, test coverage, and production ramp.
* Design and improve test fixtures and test procedures for production and failure analysis, including test software where needed.
* Own documentation for sustained designs: failure analysis reports, ECOs, troubleshooting guides, work instructions, and revision control of schematics and BOMs.
* Work across sustaining and product design teams to feed field and manufacturing learnings back into future designs.
* Collaborate with firmware and software teams to diagnose issues that span hardware and code.

**What We Are Looking For:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering.
* 8+ years of industry experience supporting production electronics, with project or program-level ownership later in your career.
* Very hands-on: strong lab fluency with scope, logic analyzer, and DMM; you trust your measurements and can debug at both the board and system level.
* Proven track record troubleshooting, root-causing, and fixing issues in deployed or in-production hardware.
* Experience working directly with manufacturing, EMS partners, and field operations teams.
* Ability to read and modify schematics and layouts in a modern ECAD tool (KiCAD, Altium, Cadence Allegro).
* Solid fundamentals across mixed-signal systems: power conversion, analog sensing, and embedded digital communication (CAN-FD, EtherCAT, SPI, I2C, USB, Ethernet, RS485).
* A juggler: comfortable managing many simultaneous issues from many stakeholders and prioritizing what matters most.
* Strong communication and people skills; you can translate between design engineers, technicians, and operations staff.
* Disciplined documentation habits: ECOs, failure analysis reports, and revision control.

**Bonus Skills:**

* Prior experience in a sustaining engineering role.
* Product lifecycle experience: supporting designs from launch through end-of-life, including obsolescence and component substitutions.
* Test engineering experience, including designing test fixtures and writing test software.
* Software development experience (Python, embedded C) for diagnostics, test automation, or firmware support.
* Experience with battery systems and battery manag

### **Minimum qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
* 5 years of experience with software development in one or more programming languages.
* 5 years of experience in one or more of the following: test automation, refactoring code, test-driven development, build infrastructure, optimizing software, debugging, building tools and testing frameworks.

### **Preferred qualifications:**

* Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science or related technical field.
* 5 years of experience with data structures/algorithms.

**About the job**
-----------------

A line of code can be many things - an amazing feature, a beautiful UI, a transformative algorithm. The faster this line of code reaches millions of users, the sooner it impacts their lives. As a Software Engineer, Tools and Infrastructure, you will be at the heart of Google’s engineering process building software that empowers engineering teams to develop and deliver high quality products quickly. We are focused on solving the hardest, most interesting challenges of developing software at scale without sacrificing stability, quality, velocity or code health.  
  
We ensure Google's success by partnering with engineering teams and developing scalable tools and infrastructure that help engineers develop, test, debug and release software quickly. We impact thousands of Googlers and billions of users by increasing the pace of product development and ensuring our products are thoroughly tested. We are advocates for code health, testability, maintainability and best practices for development and testing.  
  
Having access to all of Google's platforms and vast compute resources provides a unique opportunity to grow as an engineer. We typically work in small, nimble teams that collaborate on common problems across products and focus areas. As a result, the exposure to this broad set of problems provides technical challenges as well as accelerated career growth.

We are a multidisciplinary team working to build Fuchsia, a modern, open source operating system and adjacent open source projects like Pigweed. Pigweed is an open source collection of embedded-targeted libraries we call modules. These modules are building blocks and infrastructure that enable faster and more reliable development on small-footprint MMU-less 32-bit microcontrollers.

Fuchsia is a modern, open source operating system that is simple, secure, updatable, and performant. It’s a general purpose OS, designed to power an ecosystem of hardware and software, and provides core operating system functions like system resource management, a driver framework, and software abstractions.Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
  
  
US: $174000 - $252000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

jobs.description:
**Imagine yourself…**

* Doing meaningful work that makes an everyday impact on the world around you.
* Growing your expertise and expanding your skillset with every project.
* Contributing to a brighter, more sustainable future.

It’s possible with a role at kipp&zonen, where you’ll have the chance to shape the future of your career—and the future of our planet.

Kipp & Zonen, a Veralto company, provides class-leading instruments for measuring solar radiation and atmospheric properties in Meteorology, Climatology, Hydrology, Industry, Renewable Energy, Agriculture and Public Health.

Kipp & Zonen is the specialist in the measurement of solar and sky radiation, from the ultraviolet to the far infrared. We offer a complete range of high-quality instrumentation and accessories, from reliable cost-effective products to the best performance available. Our pyranometers, for example, are used in meteorological networks around the world.

Furthermore, our expertise and close links with the scientific community have led to high-end solutions for the measurement of atmospheric properties such as stratospheric Ozone, UV Spectra and evapo-transpiration.

Our mission is to satisfy the fundamental need to monitor atmospheric properties related to climate change, classical meteorology, agriculture, renewable energy and the available water budget.

**The opportunity:**

Reporting into the Senior Manager, R&D, you will lead the electrical engineering aspect of product development and maintenance initiatives at the Austin site and support a global organization. You will have meaningful ownership across the full product lifecycle, from ideas and prototypes to globally deployed products. This will be achieved through a hands-on role where your design judgment, hands-on efforts, production partnership, and problem-solving directly influence customer outcomes in an impactful solar market where our products shape the future of our planet. **This role is based in Austin, Texas (North Central, near the Domain), where our factory and production operations are located. It is a full‑time, onsite position (40 hours per week, Monday to Friday)**.

As a **Senior Electrical Engineer,**

* **Lead** the design, implementation, and improvement of mixed-signal and embedded electronic hardware, including schematic capture, component selection, PCB development/layout, design reviews, verification, and production release.

* **Partner** closely with firmware engineers to design, validate, and bring-up devices — taking ownership of system-level challenges and troubleshooting, driving root cause resolution, and influencing solutions that ensure reliable, scalable product performance.
* **Drive** contributions across the full product lifecycle, from ideation and prototypes to productization, manufacturing readiness, release, and ongoing sustainment — serving as a key technical voice and cross-functional resource.
* **Champion** collaboration with product management, production, test, quality, and manufacturing teams to diagnose issues, support new product introduction, and drive lasting corrective actions with measurable impact on quality and delivery outcomes.
* **Lead** technical decisions for products deployed in demanding outdoor environments, including exposure to temperature extremes, moisture, electrical transients, EMC/EMI challenges, and long lifecycle reliability requirements.

* **Identify** innovative solutions to complex hardware challenges, taking a broad perspective to influence product direction and drive cross-functional alignment on technical approaches.
* **Mentor** colleagues with less experience, acting as a go-to technical resource and actively contributing to the team's capability development.
* **Lead** regulatory and compliance activities for electrical systems, including design reviews, risk assessments, test planning, agency interactions, and support of EMC, environmental, safety, and product certification efforts.

**Essential requirements of the job include:**

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related STEM field — such as hardware engineering, computer engineering, physics, or computer science — with deep, specialized applied electrical engineering experience.
* Demonstrated experience **leading** complex hardware projects from prototype through validation and into production or field support, with a track record of delivering lasting technical outcomes across cross-functional teams. Typically 8+ years of experience in electrical engineering, with demonstrated success leading hardware development projects from concept through production and sustaining support.
* Specialized depth in PCB design, schematics, analog/digital circuits, microcontrollers, and hardware/firmware interfaces; Experience designing electronics for sensor-based products, including signal conditioning, analog front-end design, sensor integration, and measurement systems strongly preferred.
* Proven ability to interpret technical and business challenges, **recommend hardware design best practices**, and influence decisions that improve product quality, reliability, and manufacturability.
* Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to **communicate across functions**, translate complex electrical engineering concepts for technical and non-technical audiences, and champion Veralto's values of inclusion, belonging, ownership, and continuous improvement.
* Experience supporting manufacturing operations, resolving production issues, and partnering with suppliers and contract manufacturers throughout the product lifecycle.

Our collaborative, diverse team is made up of engineers and scientists, marketers and researchers; people who’ve been in the industry for decades or have just arrived with fresh ideas. We’re driven by a love of problem-solving and inventive thinking, and by the unique impact our customers make on people’s everyday lives. Bringing our global team together within our renowned brands

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager – AI/ML Hardware Engineering, Edge & AI/ML Accelerator Team
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

AWS operates the world's largest fleet of GPU-accelerated servers powering AI/ML workloads at cloud scale. Our team designs, builds, and operates this fleet — solving systemic hardware issues and building systems that detect and prevent recurrence so customers experience the highest quality of service.  
  
We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager (hardware) to drive end-to-end delivery of GPU-accelerated servers across our global fleet. You will coordinate cross-functional engineering teams spanning hardware, firmware, and software, manage ODM partnerships across multiple continents, and establish closed-loop quality systems that drive continuous improvements. This role requires technical depth to translate engineering constraints into program risk, combined with program management excellence to deliver complex hardware at global scale.  
  
What You Will Do  
You will own programs where the critical path runs through silicon, firmware, and software teams simultaneously. You will translate ambiguity into structure: turning a fleet telemetry signal into a corrective action plan with quantified failure rates, a customer requirement into a new platform milestone with EVT/DVT/PVT gates, or a manufacturing escape into a design change with updated validation criteria. You will drive decisions on program trade-offs — adjusting scope when qualification gates slip, balancing deployment speed against fleet risk, and determining when to accept interim mitigations instead of holding for root-cause fixes. When a large scale of GPU servers depend on your program landing on time, you are the one ensuring hardware readiness, qualification completeness, and operational handoff happen without gaps.  
  
Why You Will Love It  
The world's most advanced frontier models are trained on the platforms you help build. Your programs launch the GPU servers that power the largest AI/ML workloads on the planet. You will see your decisions reflected in fleet reliability metrics within weeks of deployment. The team is small and high-trust — you own programs end to end from concept through production, with direct access to leadership and engineering alike.  
  
The Ideal Candidate  
You have deep technical intuition across hardware and software — enough to challenge engineering decisions, not just track them. You thrive in ambiguity, bringing structure to programs where requirements, timelines, and dependencies are still forming. You align priorities across teams in different organizations, and you escalate with data, not noise. You actively mentor and develop others — TPMs and engineers alike. You contribute to hiring, promotion assessments, and raising the bar for program management practices in your organization.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Strategy & Mechanisms  
  

* Define program strategy, objectives, and success criteria; influence resource allocation and priority decisions across engineering workstreams to align with organizational goals
* Build and own mechanisms for program visibility — defining metrics, dashboards, and review cadences that enable data-driven decisions and early risk detection
* Streamline delivery processes across teams; identify and eliminate dependencies, redundant gates, or coordination overhead that slow velocity

  
Requirements & Planning  
  

* Facilitate requirements gathering with internal customers; develop Technical Requirements Documents (TRDs) covering server specs, rack configurations, PCIe topology, power/cooling topology, and SKU definitions
* Build program timelines aligned to different phases (Program Initiation, Design, Qualification, Pilot, Post-launch) with critical path analysis, risk identification with new & unique changes to the hardware, and milestone tracking for the program.
* Drive Program Initiation reviews: scope definition, preliminary annualized failure rate predictions, resource planning, supply chain long-lead identification, and RFP (Request for Proposal) issuance to ODMs

  
Execution & Coordination  
  

* Drive cross-functional alignment across hardware, firmware (BIOS, BMC, CPLD), software, and operations teams through design reviews, manufacturing readiness and production readiness for fleet deployment.
* Manage ODM partnerships: track EVT/DVT/PVT builds, manufacturing readiness gates, Bill of Materials (BOM) management in PLM systems, and quality checkpoints
* Identify blockers early, escalate dependencies before they impact critical path, and facilitate technical trade-off decisions across engineering workstreams.
* Communicate program status to leadership with clear reporting on milestone progress, risk posture, and mitigation plans.

  
Risk & Quality  
  

* Challenge technical workstreams to surface risks early; quantify impact to schedule and reliability (annualized failure rate targets, availability SLAs) with proposed mitigations
* Drive root cause analysis of fleet-wide hardware failures and ensure corrective actions flow back into qualification criteria and design requirements
* Define acceptance criteria, coordinate qualification testing at server and rack levels, and manage go/no-go decisions for mission-critical AI/ML workloads

  
Transition  
  

* Conduct knowledge transfer and document lessons learned; ensure operational readiness including automation, monitoring, and runbook completeness for production handoff

  
May require occasional (  
  
A day in the life  
You start the day syncing with ODM partners across time zones on build status and open engineering actions. Mid-morning, you run an engineering review connecting firmware, software, and hardware teams to unblock a qualification gate. In the afternoon, you triage a fleet reliability issue with operations data, drive alignment on corrective actions, and update executive stakeholders on program risk posture. You end the day reviewing NPI milestone readiness and ensuring the next design review has clear entry criteria.

The Automation Engineer is responsible for ensuring the reliability, availability, maintainability, recoverability, and long-term performance of industrial automation and control systems supporting manufacturing operations. The position serves as the technical reliability owner for the facility's PLCs, HMIs, industrial computers, robots, servo systems, VFDs, machine sensors, vision systems, safety controls, industrial networks, remote I/O, automated material-handling systems, and associated electrical/control infrastructure. * Serve as the technical owner for automation and controls reliability across manufacturing equipment. Develop and execute automation reliability strategies.

* Improve automation-system MTBF and MTTR.

* Establish backup, recovery, and disaster-recovery standards.
* Manage automation hardware/software lifecycle and obsolescence risk.

What You'll Bring

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Controls Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering or related technical discipline.

* Communicate and review operational performance of production equipment, and develop solutions to improve productivity.

The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices.
